value.body: Prasar Bharati is India's public service broadcaster, running All India Radio (Akashvani) and Doordarshan, including DD News and regional channels. It is a statutory autonomous body set up under the Prasar Bharati Act, 1990 (in force from 1997). It hires journalists, editors, anchors, producers and technical staff.

items.label: Akashvani broadcasting centres
items.note: As on 31 March 2025; includes 361 relay centres

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Openings are announced through Prasar Bharati notices, often for specific stations or channels, with eligibility such as a degree or diploma in journalism or mass communication plus experience and language skills. Selection is usually a written test and/or interview. Some regular news posts are filled through central services (such as the Indian Information Service) via UPSC or SSC.

value.title: At a glance
items: Many recent openings are contractual, for a fixed term, without the security of a regular government job.
Regional-language skills are an advantage for regional stations and channels.
Experience in public broadcasting is valued by other newsrooms and communication roles.
Notices are irregular, so applicants track them over time.
